title: gramark-lab-protocol
description: The typed JSON boundary the in-browser Lab (site/src/lab/) talks to across the Scala.js/Worker seam: LabRequest sent in, LabResponse returned. Hand-authored (lab/src/main/scala/gramark/lab/LabProtocol.scala's codecs have no derivation mechanism to generate this from) and validated against real serialized LabResponse output by the JVM<->JS conformance gate, so schema/code drift fails CI instead of rotting silently. labProtocolVersion 0 is draft/unstable and carries no compatibility promise.

labRequest.title: LabRequest
labRequest.description: A request from the Lab UI: the full .grmk.md source, an optional target-language input to parse, and the table-construction method to build with. Omitting `input` (or sending null) means compile-only.

method.description: Which table-construction method to build with — mirrors gramark.Method exactly.

labResponse.title: LabResponse
labResponse.description: The Lab's full response: whether the grammar itself built, any diagnostics, and — if input was given and the grammar built — the parse result.

buildOk.description: True iff the grammar compiled and its tables built with no unresolved conflicts. When false, `diagnostics` names why and `parse` is always null.

diagnostics.description: Rendered conflict/undefined-nonterminal messages (Diagnostics.renderConflicts), or a single grammar-notation parse error, when buildOk is false. Empty when buildOk is true.

parse.description: Present only when the request carried `input` and the grammar built successfully; null otherwise (compile-only requests, or any build failure).

productions.description: The Lowered Core tab's data: every flattened production of the desugared grammar. Present whenever the grammar notation parsed (Lr.parse succeeded), independent of buildOk — a grammar with genuine LR conflicts still has a well-defined production list. Null only when the grammar notation itself failed to parse.

forest.description: The All-parses tab's data: every distinct parse of `input` under the GLR multi-action table, which never fails even when the grammar has real conflicts under every method (that's exactly the ambiguous-grammar case this tab exists for, so `forest` can be populated even when buildOk is false). Present only when the request carried `input` and the grammar notation parsed; null otherwise.

productionInfo.title: ProductionInfo
productionInfo.description: One flattened production of the compiled grammar. `lhs`/`rhs` are already display-rendered (a terminal is backtick-quoted, e.g. `` `+` ``; a nonterminal is bare).

action.description: The production's raw `{% … %}` action source text, or null when the alternative has no action.

forestResult.title: ForestResult
forestResult.description: Every distinct parse of the target input, capped so a wildly ambiguous grammar can't blow up the response.

truncated.description: True when more distinct parses existed than `parses` holds.

parseResult.title: ParseResult
parseResult.description: The outcome of parsing LabRequest.input against the compiled grammar. `tokens` is populated even on a reject, so the Tokens tab still has something to show; `cst` is null unless `accepted`.

message.description: The reject reason (a lexical-error notice, or ParseError.render) when accepted is false; null when accepted.

labToken.title: LabToken
labToken.description: A single lexed token from the Lab's Tokens tab, with its source span (start/end are code-unit offsets into LabRequest.input, [start, end) — matching gramark.Spanned's own convention).

cstNode.description: The same node shape as cst-schema.json's $defs/node (Cst.toJson emits it identically here, just embedded as ParseResult.cst instead of wrapped in the {cstVersion, root} envelope that artifact's own top level adds) — kept in sync by hand, both schemas are hand-authored from the same Cst.scala encoder.
